sites_touched_JUDGEMENT: 2 files: negotiation.rs (client-to-server and server-to-client MAC selection) and cipher/mod.rs (length check)
sibling_sites_exist_JUDGEMENT: yes: both directions of MAC selection
entry_point_GUESS: Network: SSH key exchange in which both peers offer MAC 'none' together with a CTR/CBC cipher, then one crafted packet
flaw_one_line: Algorithm negotiation checks that a MAC-requiring block cipher has a MAC only in the fallback branch, so 'none' can be negotiated with AES-CTR/CBC; a short packet then panics the reader (and the session has no integrity protection).
tempting_wrong_fix_JUDGEMENT: Add a bounds check in cipher::read where the slice index panics. The crash goes away, but an unauthenticated CTR/CBC session can still be negotiated.
why_hard_or_why_control_JUDGEMENT: S2: the report and the panic point at cipher::read; the cause is in negotiation.rs. S3: the needs_mac() check existed but ran only when no common MAC was found. A fix judged only on 'no panic' passes while leaving the negotiation flaw. Rust.
caveats: No tests changed in the fix commit apart from an inline unit test; CWE listed is CWE-129 (index validation), which hides the integrity aspect. Hidden tests would need an SSH peer that offers mac=none.
